result.summary:
I wrote one spec for the group, measured at ec747b49. It is 51,178 bytes, pure ASCII, LF line endings. It sits in the gitignored .qa-s80 folder, and git status of the worktree is still empty.

The unit has no flag and changes nothing in the backend, the packages or the native folders. It covers eight changes, two of them cut back from the plan:
- C1 Home floor: a response under 300 ms goes straight to Results, otherwise the floor is 400 ms. The new leaf src/utils/clientSpeed.ts replaces HomeScreen.tsx:200 `MIN_LOADING_MS=1200`. The camera and history floors are unchanged.
- C2 Reveal cut: the measured 800 ms reveal is the ResultsScreen.tsx:460-476 winner-reveal timer, not the LoadingScreenVariants reveal stages (Home uses the concentric variant). The delay drops to 0 when the result is already in the route params at mount; history and camera keep 800.
- C3 Image prefetch: a new leaf src/services/imagePrefetch.ts prefetches at most 2 https URLs, fire-and-forget, with errors swallowed and repeats skipped. It guards the call because the jest react-native mock has no Image.prefetch.
- C4 History cache: History only. A new leaf src/services/swrCache.ts holds data in memory per user, with a 30 s throttle on focus refetches. App.tsx clears it through one effect keyed on user?.id, which covers all five sign-out paths. Every Results mount and every delete invalidate it. With no user set, every focus refetches as today, so the A12 pin stays green. authService.ts is not touched.
- Home cache cut: the Home focus refetch feeds the +bonus count on the quota pill, which is a quota surface, so it is not throttled.
- C5 metro.config.js: getSentryExpoConfig(__dirname, {includeWebReplay:false}). I measured it on the installed 7.2.0. Against the stock config it changes resolver.resolveRequest (replay modules resolve to empty), symbolicator.customizeFrame and server.enhanceMiddleware, and it adds the debug-id plugin. The cacheVersion is identical.
- C6 Lazy screens: one helper, src/navigation/lazyScreen.tsx (React.lazy plus Suspense with a null fallback), with the binding names kept so every route pin stays green. The 7 static imports it removes are Legal, Paywall, Onboarding, NewOnboardingHost, ScanCamera, InviteeQuiz and ReferralLanding.
- C7 Parallel boot read: getStableId now starts before `await getSavedLanguage()`, with a catch attached, and is awaited where it was before. Every effect keeps its order, and the B5 pin stays green. This is the only independent pair in App's init; initializeAuth's reads are left alone (auth).
- C8: freezeOnBlur on the tabs only.

Byte proxy: one offline expo export at base gave a single 6,594,787 B ios .hbc (2211 modules) that contains replay code. Dynamic imports stay in that one bundle on native, so lazy loading saves module evaluation time, not bytes.

open_questions: OQ1 LC-1 class: Legal, Paywall, Onboarding and ScanCamera are App-Review-visible screens. Their content is unchanged, but the first open may show the null Suspense fallback for one commit, which jest cannot measure. The spec classifies the unit SAFE and adds owner step 3 (a device check). The conservative alternative is to keep Legal and Paywall loading eagerly.

OQ2 Sign-out clear: rule (c) asks for one call in the existing sign-out path. The spec uses one App.tsx effect keyed on user?.id instead, which covers all five sign-out paths and every user change without touching an auth file. The alternative is one line inside authService.clearSession() (:688-699).
OQ3 Home cache: cut from CL2 because the :167 focus refetch drives the quota pill's +bonus count (quota surface). Confirm the cut, or rule a separate FOCUS unit.

OQ4 Fast-hit definition: the spec follows the brief (the result is in the route params at Results mount), which covers every Home text and URL compare. The narrower option is the Home elapsed-time band.
OQ5 Confirm that the two behavioural rows of loaderVisibility are amended as E-rows (E4/E5), rather than replaced by new RED rows.
